chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Russell Procope and Benny Carter's sleeping at the Arcadian Ballroom
summary: Procope played saxophone, clarinet and cornet with Fletcher; rumor held he led Carter to trumpet, since he led Benny's Arcadian band and played his solos while Benny slept between pillars.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Little Russ Procope. Thank goodness, he's still living, as of today anyway, you know. Procope was in Fletcher's band for years, you know. He's an excellent saxophonist and clarinetist and a very good cornetist.

In fact it got out in New York one time that Russell Procope was one of the main reasons why Benny Carter took up trumpet. I've never bought thought that, but I'll explain what I just said. You know, Benny Carter had a band in New York in the Arcadian Ballroom, and he had a big Benny there band, and they loved to have him. And that was during the time Fletcher was at Roseland, before Benny joined Fletcher. And Russell Procope was one of the members of Benny's band. And Benny Carter has always been a guy that, just like Fletcher, he did so much arranging until he was tired, you know, and he was always sleeping.

So Benny used to get all the band there sometimes and go in the Arcade 14 and go between those big pillars that used to be at the Arcadian Ballroom, which is no more now, but and go to sleep and leave he used to get between those big pillars because and he had Procope down there directing the band and playing, and Procope knew did all of Benny's solos, and he could play. He as often as he did played so much so that Benny didn't get sleepy, you see.
Oh. Got a little worried there.
